title: Wave speed formula
description: Essential: The response must correctly state the wave speed formula v = Δx / Δt and identify Δt = 0.2 s.

title: Correct propagation distance
description: Important: The reasoning must correctly relate the shift in the waveform diagram to a propagation distance of Δx = 8n + 6 meters, where n is a non-negative integer.

title: General wave speed expression
description: Essential: The final answer for part (1) must be presented as v = (40n + 30) m/s or an equivalent correct form.

title: Minimum speed identification
description: Important: For part (2), the solution must identify the minimum wave speed as corresponding to n = 0, giving v_min = 30 m/s.

title: Angular frequency calculation
description: Important: The calculation must correctly derive the angular frequency using ω = 2πv/λ, yielding ω = 15π/2 rad/s for the minimum speed.

title: Vibration equation form
description: Essential: The final answer for part (2) must be a correct vibration equation y = A sin(ωt + φ) for the particle at x=8 m, with A=0.02 m or 2 cm.

title: Initial phase determination
description: Important: The reasoning must determine the initial phase φ at t1 for x=8 m, concluding it is π radians (or equivalent, e.g., -π).

title: Unit consistency error
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the amplitude in the final vibration equation is given without units or with inconsistent units (e.g., mixing m and cm incorrectly).

title: Sign/direction misinterpretation
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the propagation distance Δx is incorrectly taken as 2 m or 8n - 6 m, misreading the waveform shift direction.
